title: Region-aware gradual load-shedding with contextual on-call runbooks
creator: Aisha Karim
description:
Goal: Reduce noisy paging and prevent region-wide overload escalation by implementing a region-aware, progressive load-shedding strategy tied to adaptive circuit-breaker hysteresis and contextual pager suppression. The change should allow degraded but functional behavior during sustained overloads, avoid unnecessary cross-region failovers, and provide on-call engineers clear, automated runbook actions for quick, low-risk remediation.

Scope: serving runtime + routing layer + alerting rules + on-call automation. Includes: 1) adaptive per-region shedding policy that progressively rejects or soft-fails low-priority requests based on queue depth, token rate, and model-specific cost; 2) circuit-breaker hysteresis tuning to avoid flip-flop during transient spikes; 3) contextual pager suppression that suppresses high-noise alerts when automated mitigation is downstream-progressing; 4) an on-call runbook with automated play triggers, manual override steps, and post-incident telemetry collection.

Out of scope: full account-level throttling policies and billing changes (handled in separate tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Net nightly pager count for regional availability SLO alerts reduced by >=40% during noisy degradation events (measured across 30-day rolling window).

On simulated sustained 2x normal load in a single region, service continues handling >=60% of high-priority requests with <2x tail latency increase, and low-priority requests are shed gracefully with explicit 429/soft-error semantics.
Circuit-breaker open/close flapping reduced to <2 state changes per 10-minute interval under synthetic burst tests.
Runbook automation correctly triggers on defined thresholds and exposes an explicit manual rollback/override path.
No false-suppression of high-severity cross-region failover alerts in canary region during rollout.
proposed_solution:
Architecture: add a region-level shedding controller in the routing plane that maintains short-window metrics (qdepth, recent token/sec, inferred cost per request) and exposes a ranked policy table for request classes (internal-critical, paid-high, free-low, background). The controller adjusts an internal shed-score and maps to one of: pass, deprioritize (background queue), soft-reject (429 with retry-after), hard-reject.

Circuit-breaker: tune thresholds with a two-stage hysteresis: (1) fast-open on sustained error-rate across multiple hosts in region; (2) delayed-close with exponentially increasing cool-down that reduces flip frequency. Use decaying EWMA for error-rate estimation to keep sensitivity to trends but resistance to noise.

Pager suppression: wire the controller into alerting so that when an automated mitigation sequence is in-progress (e.g., shedding ramping from 10%->50%), low-information availability alerts (noisy per-instance spikes) are suppressed and replaced by a single aggregated region SRE notification with a clear progress summary. Suppression must be reversible and timeboxed.

Runbook: implement an automated play that can be run by the controller for recovery (scale-up signal, temporary routing diversion to cold spare region, increase shedding threshold) and a concise manual checklist for on-call (identify region, inspect controller state, evaluate graceful rollback, escalate to infra if required).
rollout_plan:
1) Implement controller behind feature flag. 2) Unit + e2e tests in staging. 3) Canary: enable for a single low-traffic region for 48h with verbose telemetry. 4) Run synthetic 2x and spike tests while observing alert behavior. 5) Gradually enable in additional regions with 24h observation windows. 6) If any canary shows false suppression of cross-region failover alerts, immediately revert and investigate. 7) After 2-week stable run, flip flag globally and retire canary telemetry.

Safety knobs: rollout flag per-region, pause automation button in Console, explicit alert escalation if controller fails to reach mitigation targets within configured time windows.
testing_plan: Unit + integration tests for controller decision logic (qdepth -> shed-score mapping).
Chaos test: network partitions between routing plane and controller to ensure safe default (pass-through) behavior.
Load test: synthetic traffic with mixed priorities to validate graceful shedding semantics and SLO retention.
Alerting smoke tests: generate synthetic alerts to verify suppression rules and aggregated notifications are correct.
Postmortem drill in staging with runbook exercises and automated playbooks triggered to validate automation correctness.
monitoring_and_alerting_changes:
New dashboards: per-region shed-rate, pass/deprioritize/reject ratios, EWMA error-rate, circuit-breaker state timeline.

Alert changes: replace multiple per-instance availability pages with a single region-availability alert that includes a mitigation-state field (manual | automated | paused). Add a fatal-path alert that bypasses suppression and notifies on-call immediately if cross-region sync or global control plane errors detected.

Telemetry retention: 30 days for aggregated metrics, 90 days for circuit-breaker incident traces.
runbook_summary: High-level steps: 1) Identify region and check shed-rate & circuit-breaker state. 2) If automation active, review progress and ETA; allow 5-10 minutes for ramp to stabilize. 3) If automation not progressing or error-rate worsening: a) trigger manual scale-up or divert traffic to cold spare region; b) increase shedding threshold to protect critical paths; c) set a temporary suppression hold if paging noise persists and mitigation is underway. 4) If cross-region effects or data integrity risk observed, immediately disable shedding automation and escalate to SRE lead. 5) Post-incident: collect selected traces, run automated incident-summary job, and open a follow-up ticket for threshold tuning.
